How the evidence is linked

The match is a starting hypothesis. Confirm it by checking independent signals and the sample context.

01ParseRead numeric XY pairs and spectral metadata.
02DetectLocate separated maxima or minima in the trace.
03RankScore peak proximity against teaching references.
04CorroborateCompare NMR, UV, structure and sample history.

Open data & methods

Primary databases and publications used to make the workflow traceable.

PCPubChem publications & accessNCBI chemical records, identifiers and programmatic access↗ NINIST Chemistry WebBookEvaluated chemical and spectroscopic data; JCAMP downloads where available↗ SDAIST SDBSIntegrated FTIR, ¹H NMR and ¹³C NMR collections↗ NMTwenty years of nmrshiftdb2Open-access research article on NMR spectra, shifts and raw data↗ DXIUPAC JCAMP-DX recommendationStandardized exchange of machine-readable spectral data↗
Educational use: SpectraTrace ranks similarities; it does not prove identity or purity. Solvent, phase, concentration, instrument settings, baseline correction and sample preparation can shift or reshape signals. Confirm with the original database record and your instructor or laboratory workflow.
